subject: paper:winstanley-2006
quote: it has been suggested that impulsivity is not a unitary construct, but encompasses a variety of related phenomena that may differ in their biological basis.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The core claim that impulsivity fractionates into components with different biological bases.

subject: paper:nigg-2017
quote: the field needs a domain-general construct of SR that encompasses SR of action, emotion, and cognition and involves both top-down and bottom-up regulatory processes.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract; SR = self-regulation. Situates impulsivity within a self-regulation that spans action, emotion and cognition — the framing that makes an emotional (urgency) facet part of the picture.

subject: paper:jackson-mackillop-2016
quote: These findings provide robust evidence that delay discounting is significantly elevated among individuals with ADHD compared to controls.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (reused here for the choice-impulsivity facet). Meta-analytic evidence that ADHD steeply discounts delayed rewards — the delay-aversion/choice facet of impulsivity.

subject: paper:lipszyc-schachar-2010
quote: We found medium deficits in stop signal reaction time (SSRT), reflecting the speed of the inhibitory process, for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) (g = 0.62), obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) (g = 0.77) and schizophrenia (SCZ) (g = 0.69).
rationale: Verbatim (reused from the measurement note). Stop-signal inhibition deficits of comparable size across ADHD, OCD and schizophrenia — the motor-impulsivity facet is real but not ADHD-specific.

subject: paper:winstanley-2006
quote: Impulsivity, broadly defined as action without foresight, is a component of numerous psychiatric illnesses including attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), mania and substance abuse.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Names impulsivity as a component shared across ADHD, mania and substance abuse — transdiagnostic by definition.
